name: 1801 Prairie Avenue — W. W. Kimball's Chateauesque house, its massing read off J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph (T-2538; refined by T-2539, T-2540, T-1890)

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 18.000, v -11.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.454 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1801 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1801 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 storeys over a basement. The photograph shows the third of them as a storey in the roof over the main block (two storeys of wall under the cornice at about 8 m) and as a wall storey only in the south pavilion and the flank's sections, so the plan's parts below carry their own wall storeys.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'stone'.

parts.from: s28fp-1801-b1 p1 (main, stone), rectangle 1 of that part (the draft's fit); two storeys of wall under the cornice and the steep roof the Taylor photograph shows

the Taylor photograph's south pavilion: three storeys of wall under a steep coped gable facing the avenue, at the south end of the front, which the sheet carries to v 11.2 (y -3228.7); its depth back from the front is reconstructed

the Taylor photograph's three-storey section of the 18th Street flank east of the tower (print x 430-600, u 2.2-10 at the camera), its corbel table and third storey; stood 0.3 m proud of the north wall; its depth into the house is reconstructed
s28fp-1801-b1 p1, rectangle 3 of that part (the draft's fit): the photograph's gabled section with the balcony (print x 280-430), its apex about 16.3 m
s28fp-1801-b1 p1, rectangle 2 of that part (the draft's fit): the photograph's lower two-storey east range, its eaves about 8.2 m

draft_plan.note: The rectangles r1, r2 and r3 are the draft's fit inside the 1911 sheet's traced part (cell 0.25 m, 84% cover) and stay as fitted. Their wall storeys, and the two added parts, are read off the Taylor photograph through its solved camera: p_south is the front's three-storey gabled pavilion, carried to the sheet's own south line at the front (v 11.2), and p_flank the flank's three-storey section east of the tower. The two parts' depths into the house, and every roof's form behind what the camera sees, are reconstructed (L-kimball-1801-massing-2538).

draft_elevation.note: READ OFF J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph through its solved camera (data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json; heights good to about +-0.5 m near the front, +-1 m on the far flank). Principal floor 1.45 m (the stair's nine risers); the principal storey to about 5.0 m and the second to the main cornice at 8.1 m; the pavilion's and the flank's third storey to about 13.9 m, where the south gable springs (its apex about 17 m at a 58-degree pitch). The main roof: steep slate faces from the cornice to a crested deck whose front edge reads about 15.5-17 m up at the camera (the builder's 72-degree mansard with a 7.2 m lower face, its curb at 15.3 m, set so the rendered deck meets the photograph's). The tower: on the 18th Street flank, its axis 12.6 m back from the rear of the main body (8 m back from the front), between the photograph's x 698 (u 13.0) and the sheet's bump (u 12.0), its outer face 1.1 m proud of the north wall as the sheet draws it; eaves 12.9 m, cone 5.8 m to 18.7 m, finial over it; windows on its north, north-west and north-east faces. The east turret: at the flank's north-east corner on the sheet's second bump (u -15.2 to -17.9, 0.6 m proud), eaves 8.0 m with the range's, cone to 12.7 m. RECONSTRUCTED within this attribute: one radius for each tower (the photograph's tower is a shaft about 2.4 m across under a corbelled upper stage about 3.6 m across; 1.45 m splits them), the eight-sided rings, the builder's sash, dormers, stoop, chimneys and the seeded tint of its flat stand-in stone; the entrance is put at the north end of the front, under the photograph's corner loggia, which this builder cannot draw (L-kimball-1801-massing-2538).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.

research_note: REFINED IN PLACE FROM THE DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2538, piece 1 of T-1889). The draft of T-2330 stood a three-storey stone box with a round tower at the 18th Street corner, every height and feature the draft rules' reconstruction. J. W. Taylor's photograph of the house, c. 1895 (taylor_c1895_kimball_residence_1801, camera data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json), shows a different building, and this record is now written from it and from the 1911 sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1801-b1), not by the draft rules (which skip s28-1801-front): two storeys of wall under a very steep slate roof whose faces rise to a crested deck about 17 m up; the round tower standing on the 18th Street flank about 8 m back from the front, where the sheet's bump in the north wall puts it, with its cone to about 18.7 m; a three-storey pavilion under a steep stone gable at the south end of the front; a three-storey section of the flank east of the tower and a gabled section beyond it; a lower two-storey range at the east end with a small round turret at its north-east corner, where the sheet draws a second bump. It is still built by the draft builder (generators/archetypes/prairie_draft.py), because K01 cannot yet lay an all-stone house or carry a tower: T-2539 moves it onto K01 with the photograph's openings, arches and stair; T-2540 brings the roof, the flank and the rear to the photograph; T-1890 finishes the architecture. What the photograph does not show, and what this builder cannot draw, is recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md (L-kimball-1801-massing-2538) and open in the match record.
